- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if price spikes >10% from prior period, cap forecast increase at 5–7% to avoid overshoot.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, forecast should slightly dampen slope; if downward, slightly accelerate.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often lags by 1–2 days in trend direction; align forecast with sentiment momentum lagged by 1–2 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase; adjust forecast to match sentiment phase shift.
